reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates stress conversion from +50 MPa to −150 MPa in laser-AM AlSi10Mg, supporting the first two premises. However, it provides no data on fatigue improvement, the 2 mm depth, or applicability to miniature/complex geometries, and the material is AlSi10Mg, not the AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloy in the hypothesis.
premises: Ultrasonic peening converts tensile to compressive residual stresses in laser-AM parts
The stress conversion magnitude is from ~+50 MPa to ~−150 MPa
Compressive near-surface stresses enhance fatigue performance
The treatment is effective to a depth of ~2 mm
The process is applicable to miniature, complex geometries
